rules.rule_name: Clear Screen Output Fields Before Display
rules.rule_description: Before populating the card detail screen with new data, all screen output fields must be reset to ensure no residual data from a previous display is shown to the user.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen initialization process has been triggered to prepare the card detail screen for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins the screen initialization sequence
acceptance_criteria.Then: All screen output fields in the card detail screen (CCRDSLAO) are cleared by setting them to low values, ensuring no previously displayed data remains visible on the screen

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time
rules.rule_description: The system must obtain the current date and time from the system clock to display accurate temporal information on the card detail screen header.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve current system date and time

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen initialization process is preparing the card detail screen header
acceptance_criteria.When: The system needs to populate the date and time fields on the screen header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current date and time using the system's current-date function and stores it in the working storage date/time data area (WS-CURDATE-DATA) for subsequent formatting and display

rules.rule_name: Display Screen Title Line 1 on Header
rules.rule_description: The first title line of the card detail screen must be populated from the predefined application title definition to provide consistent screen identification to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Screen Title Line 1 on screen header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen initialization process is setting up the card detail screen header
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the screen header fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The first title line on the screen header (TITLE01O) is set to the predefined application title value (CCDA-TITLE01), providing the primary screen identification label to the user

rules.rule_name: Display Screen Title Line 2 on Header
rules.rule_description: The second title line of the card detail screen must be populated from the predefined application title definition to provide complete screen identification to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Screen Title Line 2 on screen header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen initialization process is setting up the card detail screen header
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the screen header fields after setting Title Line 1
acceptance_criteria.Then: The second title line on the screen header (TITLE02O) is set to the predefined application secondary title value (CCDA-TITLE02), providing the secondary screen identification label to the user

rules.rule_name: Display Current Transaction ID on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The transaction identifier for the current screen must be displayed in the screen header so the user can identify which transaction they are currently executing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Transaction ID on screen header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen initialization process is setting up the card detail screen header
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the transaction identification field on the screen header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction name field on the screen header (TRNNAMEO) is set to the current transaction ID value (LIT-THISTRANID), allowing the user to identify the active transaction

rules.rule_name: Display Current Program Name on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The name of the currently executing program must be displayed in the screen header to provide the user with context about which program is handling their request.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Program Name on screen header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen initialization process is setting up the card detail screen header
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the program identification field on the screen header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program name field on the screen header (PGMNAMEO) is set to the current program name value (LIT-THISPGM), allowing the user to identify the active program

rules.rule_name: Format Current Date as MM-DD-YY for Screen Display
rules.rule_description: The current system date must be formatted into the standard MM-DD-YY display format by extracting the month, day, and two-digit year components separately before being shown on the screen header.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format current date as MM-DD-YY

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current system date has been retrieved and stored in the working storage date area (WS-CURDATE-DATA)

rules.rule_name: Set Formatted Date on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The date formatted in MM-DD-YY format must be placed into the screen header date display field so the user can see the current date while using the card detail screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set formatted date on screen header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current date has been formatted into MM-DD-YY format and stored in WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the date field on the screen header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The formatted date value from WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY is moved to the screen header date output field (CURDATEO) of the card detail screen (CCRDSLAO), displaying the current date to the user in MM-DD-YY format

rules.rule_name: Format Current Time as HH-MM-SS for Screen Display
rules.rule_description: The current system time must be formatted into the standard HH-MM-SS display format by extracting the hours, minutes, and seconds components separately before being shown on the screen header.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Format current time as HH-MM-SS

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current system time has been retrieved and stored in the working storage date/time area (WS-CURDATE-DATA)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system formats the time for screen header display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system extracts the hours component into WS-CURTIME-HH, the minutes component into WS-CURTIME-MM, and the seconds component into WS-CURTIME-SS, composing the time in HH-MM-SS format stored in WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS

rules.rule_name: Set Formatted Time on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The time formatted in HH-MM-SS format must be placed into the screen header time display field so the user can see the current time while using the card detail screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set formatted time on screen header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current time has been formatted into HH-MM-SS format and stored in WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets the time field on the screen header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The formatted time value from WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS is moved to the screen header time output field (CURTIMEO) of the card detail screen (CCRDSLAO), displaying the current time to the user in HH-MM-SS format

rules.rule_name: Populate Card Expiration Month on Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has been successfully retrieved from the card file and the FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT condition is TRUE

rules.rule_name: Populate Card Expiration Year on Screen

rules.rule_name: Populate Card Active Status on Screen
rules.rule_description: When a card record has been successfully retrieved, the current active or inactive status of the card is displayed on the card detail screen.

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card record has been successfully retrieved from the card file and the FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT condition is TRUE

rules.rule_name: Default Screen Prompt When No Informational Message Exists

rules.rule_name: Retain Existing Informational Message When Already Set

rules.rule_name: Display Default Prompt Message on Screen
rules.rule_description: When no informational message is set, the default prompt instructing the user to enter Account and Card Number is displayed in the informational message area on the screen, and the info message display area is visually dimmed to indicate it is a system-generated default prompt rather than an active informational message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display prompt message on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen prompt has been defaulted to 'Enter Account and Card Number' because no informational message was set (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE is true)
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen attributes and message fields are being finalized for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The prompt message (WS-INFO-MSG containing the default prompt) is moved to the informational message display field (INFOMSGO) on the screen, AND the informational message display area is rendered in a dimmed/dark visual attribute (DFHBMDAR) to distinguish it as a default system prompt

rules.rule_name: Display Existing Informational Message on Screen
rules.rule_description: When an informational message has been set in the session, it is displayed in the informational message area on the screen with a neutral visual style, indicating it is an active system-generated informational message for the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display informational message on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: An informational message is currently set in the session (WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE is false, meaning WS-INFO-MSG contains content)
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen attributes and message fields are being finalized for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The existing informational message (WS-INFO-MSG) is moved to the informational message display field (INFOMSGO) on the screen, AND the informational message display area is rendered in a neutral visual attribute (DFHNEUTR) to present it as an active informational message to the user

rules.rule_name: Default Prompt on First-Time Screen Entry
rules.rule_description: When the screen is displayed for the very first time in a new session (no prior communication area exists), the system automatically sets the default prompt to instruct the user to enter their Account ID and Card Number, ensuring the user is guided on what input is required from the start.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Default screen prompt to: 'Enter Account and Card Number'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display for the first time with no existing session data (EIBCALEN equals zero, indicating no prior communication area)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets up the screen variables for initial display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen prompt is defaulted to instruct the user to enter Account and Card Number (WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT is set to TRUE), so the user is immediately guided to provide the required search criteria

rules.rule_name: Display Error or Return Message in Screen Error Field

acceptance_criteria.When: The screen output fields are being populated in preparation for sending the screen to the user terminal

rules.rule_name: Display Informational Message in Screen Info Field

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display informational message in screen info message field for user feedback

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card detail screen is being prepared for display after any processing step, and the informational message field (WS-INFO-MSG) either contains an informational text or is empty/blank

acceptance_criteria.Then: The current value of the informational message (WS-INFO-MSG) is moved directly to the screen informational message output field (INFOMSGO): if WS-INFO-MSG contains a message, that informational text is displayed in the info message area of the screen; if WS-INFO-MSG is blank or spaces, the screen informational message field is displayed as blank, showing no informational content to the user

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card detail screen is being set up for display and the system has a record of the last mapset visited and the originating program name

acceptance_criteria.Then: If both conditions are true, the Account ID and Card Number fields are set to protected (read-only) mode; if either or both conditions are false, both fields are set to editable mode allowing user input

rules.rule_name: Protect Account ID and Card Number Fields When Arriving from Card List
rules.rule_description: When a user arrives at the card detail screen by selecting a record from the Card List screen, the Account ID and Card Number fields must be made read-only to preserve the integrity of the selection made on the list. acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor is automatically positioned on the Card Number input field so the user can immediately correct the invalid card number

rules.rule_name: Position Cursor on Card Number Field When Card Filter is Blank

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Card Filter Invalid or Blank? → Yes - Invalid or Blank Card Number → Position Cursor on Card Number Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the Credit Card Detail screen, the Account ID is valid, and the user has submitted the screen without providing a Card Number value (Card Filter is marked as BLANK — field was empty, spaces, zeros, or asterisk)

acceptance_criteria.Then: The cursor is automatically positioned on the Card Number input field so the user is directed to enter the required card number

rules.rule_name: Record Current Screen as Next Navigation Destination
rules.rule_description: When the credit card detail screen is about to be transmitted to the user terminal, the system records the current screen's map name and mapset name as the designated next navigation destination, ensuring the application knows which screen to return to on the next user interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record current screen map and mapset as the next navigation destination

acceptance_criteria.Given: The credit card detail screen transmission process has been initiated and the system is preparing to display the screen to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen transmission step (1400-SEND-SCREEN) is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current credit card detail screen map name (LIT-THISMAP) must be recorded as the next map destination (CCARD-NEXT-MAP), and the current credit card detail screen mapset name (LIT-THISMAPSET) must be recorded as the next mapset destination (CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET), so that the application retains the correct screen context for subsequent navigation

rules.rule_name: Mark Program State as Re-Enter for Next User Interaction
rules.rule_description: Immediately before sending the credit card detail screen to the user, the program state flag must be set to RE-ENTER mode. This ensures that when the user next interacts with the screen (e.g., presses ENTER), the system correctly identifies the interaction as a return to an already-displayed screen and routes processing through the input validation and data retrieval path rather than the initial entry path.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Mark program state as RE-ENTER so next interaction knows user is returning to this screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The credit card detail screen is being prepared for transmission to the user terminal
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen transmission step (1400-SEND-SCREEN) is executed prior to sending the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program state indicator (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER) must be set to TRUE, so that the next user interaction with this screen is processed as a re-entry, triggering input validation (2000-PROCESS-INPUTS) rather than a fresh program entry flow

rules.rule_name: Send Formatted Credit Card Detail Screen with Cursor Positioned on Relevant Input Field
rules.rule_description: The fully formatted credit card detail screen, containing all populated data fields (account ID, card number, card name, expiry month, expiry year, card status, error messages, info messages, date, time, titles), must be transmitted to the user's terminal. The cursor must be automatically positioned on the relevant input field as determined by the screen attribute setup (e.g., on the Account ID field if it is in error or blank, on the Card Number field if it is in error or blank, or defaulting to the Account ID field).
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Send formatted credit card detail screen to user terminal with cursor positioned on relevant input field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The credit card detail screen output area (CCRDSLAO) has been fully populated with account ID, card number, card embossed name, expiry month, expiry year, card active status, error messages, informational messages, current date, current time, transaction name, and program name; and screen field attributes (colors, protection, cursor position) have been set based on validation outcomes
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen transmission command is issued using the recorded next map (CCARD-NEXT-MAP) and next mapset (CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET) with the CURSOR option
acceptance_criteria.Then: The formatted screen (CCRDSLAO) must be sent to the user terminal with the cursor automatically placed on the input field designated during screen attribute setup (Account ID field if account is invalid or blank; Card Number field if card is invalid or blank; otherwise defaulting to Account ID field), allowing the user to immediately interact with the correct field

rules.rule_name: Clear Previous Screen Content and Unlock Keyboard for User Interaction
rules.rule_description: When transmitting the credit card detail screen, any previously displayed screen content on the user's terminal must be fully erased and replaced with the new screen content. Additionally, the terminal keyboard must be unlocked (freed) after the screen is sent, enabling the user to type input or press function keys to interact with the newly displayed credit card detail screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear previous screen content and unlock keyboard so user can interact with the screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The credit card detail screen is being transmitted to the user terminal and the terminal may currently be displaying a previous screen with locked keyboard
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen transmission command is issued with the ERASE and FREEKB options
acceptance_criteria.Then: All previously displayed content on the user terminal screen must be completely erased and replaced with the new credit card detail screen content, and the terminal keyboard must be unlocked (freed) so the user can immediately enter data or press function keys (ENTER or PF3) to interact with the screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Credit Card Detail Search Screen has been previously displayed to the user and the user has submitted the screen by pressing ENTER
acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects that the program is in a re-entry state (the user is returning to the program after the screen was sent to them for input)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system initiates the input processing sequence, beginning with receiving the data the user entered on the Credit Card Detail Search Screen, followed by validating those inputs

rules.rule_name: Receive User-Entered Data from Credit Card Detail Search Screen
rules.rule_description: The system reads and captures all data entered by the user on the Credit Card Detail Search Screen into the designated screen input area so that it can be subsequently validated and processed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Receive User Input from Credit Card Detail Search Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the Credit Card Detail Search Screen with data entered in the Account ID and/or Card Number fields

rules.rule_name: Store Received Input Data in Screen Input Area for Processing
rules.rule_description: Once the user's submitted data is received from the Credit Card Detail Search Screen, it is held in the screen input area (CCRDSLAI) as the authoritative source of the user's input values, ready to be passed to the validation step.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Input Data Stored in Screen Input Area for Processing

acceptance_criteria.When: The receive map operation completes and the input data is stored in the screen input area (CCRDSLAI)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account ID value entered by the user is available in the Account ID input field (ACCTSIDI of CCRDSLAI) and the Card Number value entered by the user is available in the Card Number input field (CARDSIDI of CCRDSLAI), and the system proceeds to the input validation step (2200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS)

rules.rule_name: Proceed to Input Validation After Data Reception
rules.rule_description: After the user's input data has been received and stored from the Credit Card Detail Search Screen, the system immediately proceeds to validate the captured input values before any data retrieval is attempted.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user's submitted data has been received from the Credit Card Detail Search Screen and stored in the screen input area (CCRDSLAI)

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system automatically proceeds to the input validation step (2200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS) to validate the Account ID and Card Number values entered by the user, without any further user interaction required at this stage

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Account Number blank or zero?

rules.rule_name: Account Number Missing - Prompt Message Assignment
rules.rule_description: When the account number is found to be blank or zero, the system sets a user-facing prompt message to guide the user to enter an account number, but only if no prior error or return message has already been set during this processing cycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Prompt Message: Please Enter Account Number

rules.rule_name: Account ID Cleared from Session When Blank

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Number field has been determined to be blank or zero

rules.rule_name: Account Number Non-Numeric Value Detection
rules.rule_description: When the user provides an account number that contains non-numeric characters, the system detects the invalid format and flags both an input error and the account filter as invalid, preventing a data lookup with a malformed account number.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Account Number non-numeric?

rules.rule_name: Account Number Non-Numeric - Error Message Assignment

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Number field contains a non-numeric value, triggering an input error
acceptance_criteria.When: No prior error or return message has already been set for this screen interaction (message flag is OFF)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error message to 'ACCOUNT FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 11 DIGIT NUMBER' to inform the user of the correct format requirement; if a message was already set, no new message is assigned and the existing message is preserved

rules.rule_name: Account ID Cleared from Session When Non-Numeric
rules.rule_description: When the account number is found to be non-numeric, the previously stored Account ID in the session context is cleared to zero, ensuring no invalid account data persists in the session for subsequent processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear Account ID from Session Context

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Account Number field has been determined to contain a non-numeric value
acceptance_criteria.When: The non-numeric account validation error path is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Account ID stored in the session communication area (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) is set to zero, removing any previously held account value, and account number validation ends immediately without further checks

rules.rule_name: Valid Account Number Stored in Session
rules.rule_description: When the account number passes all validation checks (non-blank, non-zero, and fully numeric), it is accepted as a valid account filter, stored in the session context for use in card data retrieval, and the account filter is marked as valid for downstream processing.

acceptance_criteria.Then: The validated Account Number is stored in the session communication area (CDEMO-ACCT-ID) for use in subsequent card data lookup, and the Account Filter status is marked as 'VALID' (FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID), allowing the card retrieval process to proceed

rules.rule_name: Display Prompt Message When Card Number is Missing and No Prior Error Message Exists

rules.rule_name: Clear Card Number in Communication Area When Card is Blank

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Card Number field has been identified as blank, spaces, or zero

rules.rule_name: Reject Non-Numeric Card Number Entry

rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is Card Number non-numeric?

rules.rule_name: Display Specific Error Message for Non-Numeric Card Number When No Prior Message Exists

rules.rule_name: Error Message Propagation to Screen Display Field

acceptance_criteria.Then: The current value of the working storage return message field (WS-RETURN-MSG) must be moved to the screen error message display field (CCARD-ERROR-MSG), ensuring the user sees the correct message — whether it is an error description, a prompt, or blank — on the next screen display

rules.rule_name: Application-Level Communication Area Packaging
rules.rule_description: Before returning to CICS, the application-level communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), which holds shared application state such as account ID, card number, program navigation context, and user type, must be copied into the first portion of the combined outbound communication area to preserve application-wide session state across interactions.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to return control to CICS after completing a processing cycle, and the application-level communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) contains the current application state including account ID, card number, navigation context (from/to program and transaction), user type, and program re-entry flag
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the return sequence (COMMON-RETURN)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The entire content of the application-level communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) must be placed into the beginning (first segment) of the combined outbound communication area (WS-COMMAREA), preserving all application-wide session data for the next interaction

rules.rule_name: Program-Specific Communication Area Appended After Application Commarea
rules.rule_description: The program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA), which holds state data specific to this card detail screen program, must be appended immediately after the application-level communication area within the combined outbound communication area. The offset position is calculated as the length of the application commarea plus one, ensuring no overlap and correct retrieval on the next entry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Append program-specific commarea into combined communication area after application commarea

acceptance_criteria.Given: The application-level communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) has already been placed into the first segment of the combined communication area (WS-COMMAREA), and the program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) contains state data specific to this card detail screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the return sequence (COMMON-RETURN) and packages the outbound communication area
acceptance_criteria.Then: The content of the program-specific communication area (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) must be written into the combined communication area (WS-COMMAREA) starting at the position immediately after the end of the application commarea — specifically at offset (LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + 1) for a length equal to (LENGTH OF WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) — so that both areas are stored contiguously without overlap for correct restoration on the next program entry

rules.rule_name: Session Continuity Preservation on Return to CICS
rules.rule_description: After packaging all session state, the system must return control to CICS specifying the current transaction ID so that the same transaction is re-invoked when the user next interacts with the screen, and passing the fully packaged combined communication area so all session context is available for the next processing cycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Return to CICS with current transaction ID and packaged communication area for next user interaction

acceptance_criteria.Given: The combined communication area (WS-COMMAREA) has been fully packaged with both the application-level commarea and the program-specific commarea, and the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) identifies this card detail screen transaction
acceptance_criteria.When: The system completes the return sequence (COMMON-RETURN) and issues the CICS RETURN command
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control must be returned to CICS with: (1) the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) specified as the next transaction to be invoked upon the user's next action, (2) the fully packaged combined communication area (WS-COMMAREA) passed as the communication area, and (3) the length of the combined communication area specified — ensuring the complete session state (application context, program-specific state, navigation history, account and card data) is preserved and available when the user next interacts with the screen

acceptance_criteria.When: The unexpected scenario handling assigns a classification code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error code is set to '0001' to specifically flag and classify this condition as an unexpected data scenario

rules.rule_name: Clear Prior Error Reason to Avoid Misleading Context
rules.rule_description: When handling an unexpected program state, any previously recorded error reason is cleared (set to blank spaces) to ensure that stale or unrelated error context from prior operations does not mislead the error record for this new unexpected scenario.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear any prior error reason to avoid misleading context

acceptance_criteria.Given: An unrecognized program state has been detected and error code '0001' has been assigned
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the error context for the unexpected scenario
acceptance_criteria.Then: Any previously stored error reason detail is cleared to blank spaces so that no prior unrelated error reason is associated with this unexpected scenario

rules.rule_name: Set User-Facing Error Message for Unexpected Scenario
rules.rule_description: When an unexpected program state is encountered, the system sets the error message to the specific text 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO' which will be presented to the user to communicate that an unrecognized condition has occurred.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set error message to 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO' for user display

acceptance_criteria.Given: An unrecognized program state has been detected, the responsible program has been recorded, error code '0001' has been assigned, and prior error reason has been cleared
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the message to be shown to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The return message displayed to the user is set to the exact text 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO'

rules.rule_name: Display Unexpected Scenario Error Message to User
rules.rule_description: After setting the 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO' error message, the system immediately displays this message as plain text on the user's terminal screen and terminates the current program execution, ensuring the user is informed of the unrecoverable unexpected condition.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display error message to user terminal

acceptance_criteria.Given: The error message has been set to 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO' and all error tracking fields have been populated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the error information to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO' message is displayed as plain text on the user's terminal screen and the program ends, preventing any further processing under the unrecognized state

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Credit Card Detail screen program is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins execution
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All working storage areas (CC-WORK-AREA, WS-MISC-STORAGE, WS-COMMAREA) are initialized to their default values, the current transaction ID is set to LIT-THISTRANID in WS-TRANID, and the return message flag (WS-RETURN-MSG) is set to OFF

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Initialization on Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: On every entry to the Credit Card Detail screen program, all working storage areas, communication areas, and the return message flag are initialized, and the current transaction ID is set.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Credit Card Detail screen program is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.When: There is no prior communication area data (EIBCALEN equals zero) OR the calling program is the main menu program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM equals LIT-MENUPGM) AND the program re-entry flag is NOT set (NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Both CARDDEMO-COMMAREA and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA are initialized to their default values, clearing any previously stored account ID, card number, and program context

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fresh Session Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is invoked for the first time with no prior session data, or when navigating from the main menu without a re-entry flag, all communication areas are reset to start a clean session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Credit Card Detail screen program is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.When: There is prior communication area data (EIBCALEN is not zero) AND the conditions for a fresh start are not met
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: CARDDEMO-COMMAREA is restored from the first portion of DFHCOMMAREA (length of CARDDEMO-COMMAREA bytes), and WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA is restored from the subsequent portion of DFHCOMMAREA (starting after CARDDEMO-COMMAREA, for the length of WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA), preserving account ID, card number, and all program context

all_rules.Rule_Name: Returning Session Data Restoration
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user is returning to the Credit Card Detail screen with an existing session, previously stored data including account ID, card number, and program context are restored from the communication area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Credit Card Detail screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key (ENTER, CLEAR, PA1, PA2, PF1 through PF24)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The corresponding action indicator flag is set: ENTER sets CCARD-AID-ENTER, CLEAR sets CCARD-AID-CLEAR, PA1 sets CCARD-AID-PA1, PA2 sets CCARD-AID-PA2, PF1/PF13 set CCARD-AID-PFK01, PF2/PF14 set CCARD-AID-PFK02, PF3/PF15 set CCARD-AID-PFK03, PF4/PF16 set CCARD-AID-PFK04, PF5/PF17 set CCARD-AID-PFK05, PF6/PF18 set CCARD-AID-PFK06, PF7/PF19 set CCARD-AID-PFK07, PF8/PF20 set CCARD-AID-PFK08, PF9/PF21 set CCARD-AID-PFK09, PF10/PF22 set CCARD-AID-PFK10, PF11/PF23 set CCARD-AID-PFK11, PF12/PF24 set CCARD-AID-PFK12

all_rules.Rule_Name: Function Key Capture and PF13-PF24 Mapping
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program captures the function key pressed by the user and maps it to a corresponding action indicator. PF13 through PF24 are treated as equivalents to PF01 through PF12 respectively.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Credit Card Detail screen and has pressed a key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key pressed is neither ENTER (CCARD-AID-ENTER) nor PF3 (CCARD-AID-PFK03)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key is marked as invalid (PFK-INVALID is TRUE), and the action is overridden to ENTER (CCARD-AID-ENTER is set to TRUE), so the screen processes the input as if the user pressed ENTER

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Key Default to Enter Behavior
all_rules.Rule_Description: Only the ENTER key and PF3 are recognized as valid actions on the Credit Card Detail screen. Any other key pressed is overridden and treated as if the user pressed ENTER.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Credit Card Detail screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF3
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If CDEMO-FROM-TRANID is LOW-VALUES or SPACES, the destination transaction is set to LIT-MENUTRANID (main menu transaction); otherwise CDEMO-FROM-TRANID is used as the destination transaction. If CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is LOW-VALUES or SPACES, the destination program is set to LIT-MENUPGM (main menu program); otherwise CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM is used as the destination program. The current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) is recorded as CDEMO-FROM-TRANID, the current program (LIT-THISPGM) is recorded as CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM, user type is set to CDEMO-USRTYP-USER, program state is set to CDEMO-PGM-ENTER, and the current mapset (LIT-THISMAPSET) and map (LIT-THISMAP) are recorded in CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET and CDEMO-LAST-MAP

all_rules.Rule_Name: PF3 Back Navigation - Determine Return Destination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 to exit the Credit Card Detail screen, the program determines the correct destination to return to based on whether a calling program and transaction are recorded in the session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF3 and the return destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) has been determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Control transfer is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is transferred to CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM via XCTL, passing CARDDEMO-COMMAREA as the communication area, and the current program terminates

all_rules.Rule_Name: PF3 Transfer Control to Calling Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: After determining the return destination, the program transfers control to the target program passing the full communication area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in first-entry state (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The calling program is the Credit Card List program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM equals LIT-CCLISTPGM)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Input status is set to INPUT-OK, CDEMO-ACCT-ID is moved to CC-ACCT-ID-N, CDEMO-CARD-NUM is moved to CC-CARD-NUM-N, card data retrieval is performed (9000-READ-DATA), and the card detail screen is displayed (1000-SEND-MAP)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Direct Entry from Credit Card List Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user navigates to the Credit Card Detail screen directly from the Credit Card List screen, the account ID and card number are automatically carried over from the list selection and card data is immediately retrieved without requiring manual entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in first-entry state (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The calling program is NOT the Credit Card List program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM does not equal LIT-CCLISTPGM)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card detail screen is displayed (1000-SEND-MAP) with empty input fields, prompting the user to enter an Account ID and Card Number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initial Screen Display on First Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user enters the Credit Card Detail screen for the first time from any source other than the Credit Card List screen, a blank search screen is displayed prompting the user to enter search criteria.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is in re-entry state (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE), indicating the user has previously seen the screen and submitted data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses ENTER to submit the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Input processing is performed (2000-PROCESS-INPUTS). If INPUT-ERROR is set, the screen is re-displayed with error highlights (1000-SEND-MAP) and processing returns to await further input. If no INPUT-ERROR, card data retrieval is performed (9000-READ-DATA) followed by screen display (1000-SEND-MAP)

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Input Processing on Re-Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user submits data on the Credit Card Detail screen, the inputs are received and validated. If valid, card data is retrieved and displayed; if invalid, the screen is re-displayed with error indicators.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered data on the Credit Card Detail screen and pressed ENTER
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Input processing begins (2000-PROCESS-INPUTS is performed)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen data is received from the terminal into CCRDSLAI using the current map (LIT-THISMAP) and mapset (LIT-THISMAPSET), making the entered Account ID (ACCTSIDI) and Card Number (CARDSIDI) available for validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Input Reception from Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: The data entered by the user on the Credit Card Detail search screen is received into the program's input area for subsequent validation and processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Screen input has been received into CCRDSLAI
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Input normalization is performed during edit processing (2200-EDIT-MAP-INPUTS)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If ACCTSIDI of CCRDSLAI equals '*' or SPACES, CC-ACCT-ID is set to LOW-VALUES; otherwise CC-ACCT-ID is set to the value of ACCTSIDI. If CARDSIDI of CCRDSLAI equals '*' or SPACES, CC-CARD-NUM is set to LOW-VALUES; otherwise CC-CARD-NUM is set to the value of CARDSIDI

all_rules.Rule_Name: Input Field Normalization - Asterisk and Space Handling
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before validation, input fields containing asterisk or space characters are normalized to low-values, treating them as blank/empty entries.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Input normalization has been completed and account validation (2210-EDIT-ACCOUNT) is being performed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: CC-ACCT-ID equals LOW-VALUES or SPACES, or CC-ACCT-ID-N (numeric form) equals ZEROS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: INPUT-ERROR is set to TRUE, FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK is set to TRUE, FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is set to TRUE, CDEMO-ACCT-ID is set to ZEROES, and if no prior return message exists (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF), WS-PROMPT-FOR-ACCT is set to TRUE to prompt the user to enter an account number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Number Blank Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Number field is validated to ensure it has been provided. If blank or zero, an input error is raised and the user is prompted to enter an account number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Number field (CC-ACCT-ID) is not blank and not zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: CC-ACCT-ID contains non-numeric characters (IS NOT NUMERIC)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: INPUT-ERROR is set to TRUE, FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is set to TRUE, CDEMO-ACCT-ID is set to ZERO, and if no prior return message exists (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF), the error message 'ACCOUNT FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 11 DIGIT NUMBER' is placed in WS-RETURN-MSG

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Number Numeric Format Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Number must be a numeric value. If non-numeric characters are entered, an error message is displayed indicating the required format.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Number field (CC-ACCT-ID) is not blank, not zero, and is numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Account validation (2210-EDIT-ACCOUNT) completes successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: CC-ACCT-ID is moved to CDEMO-ACCT-ID in the session communication area, and FLG-ACCTFILTER-ISVALID is set to TRUE

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Number Valid - Save to Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Account Number passes all validation checks, it is saved to the session communication area and marked as valid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Input normalization has been completed and card validation (2220-EDIT-CARD) is being performed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: CC-CARD-NUM equals LOW-VALUES or SPACES, or CC-CARD-NUM-N (numeric form) equals ZEROS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: INPUT-ERROR is set to TRUE, FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK is set to TRUE, FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK is set to TRUE, CDEMO-CARD-NUM is set to ZEROES, and if no prior return message exists (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF), WS-PROMPT-FOR-CARD is set to TRUE to prompt the user to enter a card number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Number Blank Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Card Number field is validated to ensure it has been provided. If blank or zero, an input error is raised and the user is prompted to enter a card number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Number field (CC-CARD-NUM) is not blank and not zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: CC-CARD-NUM contains non-numeric characters (IS NOT NUMERIC)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: INPUT-ERROR is set to TRUE, FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK is set to TRUE, CDEMO-CARD-NUM is set to ZERO, and if no prior return message exists (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF), the error message 'CARD ID FILTER,IF SUPPLIED MUST BE A 16 DIGIT NUMBER' is placed in WS-RETURN-MSG

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Number Numeric Format Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Card Number must be a numeric value. If non-numeric characters are entered, an error message is displayed indicating the required format.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Card Number field (CC-CARD-NUM) is not blank, not zero, and is numeric
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Card validation (2220-EDIT-CARD) completes successfully
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: CC-CARD-NUM-N (numeric form) is moved to CDEMO-CARD-NUM in the session communication area, and FLG-CARDFILTER-ISVALID is set to TRUE

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Number Valid - Save to Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Card Number passes all validation checks, it is saved to the session communication area and marked as valid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both Account Number validation (2210-EDIT-ACCOUNT) and Card Number validation (2220-EDIT-CARD) have been performed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK is TRUE AND FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK is TRUE (both fields were left empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: NO-SEARCH-CRITERIA-RECEIVED is set to TRUE, indicating the user has not provided any search parameters to retrieve card details

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cross-Field Validation - No Search Criteria Provided
all_rules.Rule_Description: After individual field validations, a cross-field check ensures that at least one search criterion has been provided. If both Account Number and Card Number are blank, a no-search-criteria condition is raised.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Input validation has passed (no INPUT-ERROR) and card data retrieval (9000-READ-DATA / 9100-GETCARD-BYACCTCARD) is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The card record lookup is performed against the CARDDAT file (LIT-CARDFILENAME)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Card Number (CC-CARD-NUM) is used as the record identifier (WS-CARD-RID-CARDNUM) to read the CARD-RECORD from the CARDDAT VSAM file, retrieving the full card record including embossed name, expiry date, and active status

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Record Retrieval by Card Number
all_rules.Rule_Description: Card details are retrieved from the CARDDAT file using the Card Number as the primary lookup key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card record lookup has been performed against the CARDDAT file using the Card Number
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file read returns a normal (successful) response
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT is set to TRUE, enabling the card details (embossed name, expiry month, expiry year, active status) to be populated on the display screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Card Record Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card record is successfully located in the CARDDAT file, the result is marked as found so the card details can be displayed on screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card record lookup has been performed against the CARDDAT file using the Card Number
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file read returns a not-found response (record does not exist)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: INPUT-ERROR is set to TRUE, FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is set to TRUE, FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK is set to TRUE, and if no prior return message exists (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF), DID-NOT-FIND-ACCTCARD-COMBO is set to TRUE to display a message indicating the Account/Card combination was not found

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Record Not Found Handling
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no card record is found matching the provided Card Number, an error condition is raised on both the Account and Card Number fields, and a not-found message is displayed to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen is being prepared for display (1100-SCREEN-INIT is performed)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Screen initialization executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen output area (CCRDSLAO) is cleared to LOW-VALUES, CCDA-TITLE01 is moved to TITLE01O, CCDA-TITLE02 is moved to TITLE02O, LIT-THISTRANID is moved to TRNNAMEO, LIT-THISPGM is moved to PGMNAMEO, the current date is formatted as MM/DD/YY (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) and moved to CURDATEO, and the current time is formatted as HH:MM:SS (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) and moved to CURTIMEO

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Header Initialization with Date and Time
all_rules.Rule_Description: Every time the Credit Card Detail screen is prepared for display, the screen header is populated with the application titles, current transaction ID, program name, current date in MM/DD/YY format, and current time in HH:MM:SS format.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen variables are being set up (1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS) and EIBCALEN is not zero (returning session)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Account ID display setup executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If CDEMO-ACCT-ID equals zero, ACCTSIDO of CCRDSLAO is set to LOW-VALUES (field cleared); otherwise CC-ACCT-ID is moved to ACCTSIDO of CCRDSLAO to display the account ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account ID Field Population on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account ID field on the screen is populated from the session data. If no account ID is present, the field is cleared.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen variables are being set up (1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS) and EIBCALEN is not zero (returning session)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Card Number display setup executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If CDEMO-CARD-NUM equals zero, CARDSIDO of CCRDSLAO is set to LOW-VALUES (field cleared); otherwise CC-CARD-NUM is moved to CARDSIDO of CCRDSLAO to display the card number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Number Field Population on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Card Number field on the screen is populated from the session data. If no card number is present, the field is cleared.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen variables are being set up (1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: FOUND-CARDS-FOR-ACCOUNT is TRUE (a card record was successfully retrieved)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: CARD-EMBOSSED-NAME is moved to CRDNAMEO of CCRDSLAO, CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE is moved to CARD-EXPIRAION-DATE-X, CARD-EXPIRY-MONTH is moved to EXPMONO of CCRDSLAO, CARD-EXPIRY-YEAR is moved to EXPYEARO of CCRDSLAO, and CARD-ACTIVE-STATUS is moved to CRDSTCDO of CCRDSLAO

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Details Population on Screen After Successful Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card record has been successfully retrieved, the card details including the cardholder name, expiry month, expiry year, and active status are displayed on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen variables are being set up (1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: EIBCALEN equals zero (first-time display) OR WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE is TRUE (no informational message available)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: WS-PROMPT-FOR-INPUT is set to TRUE, directing the screen to display a prompt message asking the user to enter Account ID and Card Number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Prompt Message for Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the screen is displayed for the first time or when there is no informational message to show, the screen defaults to prompting the user to enter their search criteria.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen variables are being set up (1200-SETUP-SCREEN-VARS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Screen variable setup completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: WS-RETURN-MSG is moved to ERRMSGO of CCRDSLAO (error message area), and WS-INFO-MSG is moved to INFOMSGO of CCRDSLAO (informational message area)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error and Informational Message Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current error/return message and informational message are always moved to their respective screen output fields before the screen is sent to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Screen attributes are being set up (1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The last mapset (CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET) equals LIT-CCLISTMAPSET AND the calling program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) equals LIT-CCLISTPGM (Credit Card List screen)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: ACCTSIDA of CCRDSLAI is set to DFHBMPRF (protected) and CARDSIDA of CCRDSLAI is set to DFHBMPRF (protected), preventing the user from modifying these fields. Otherwise (any other source), ACCTSIDA is set to DFHBMFSE (editable) and CARDSIDA is set to DFHBMFSE (editable)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Field Protection Based on Navigation Source
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account ID and Card Number fields are set as protected (read-only) when the user arrives from the Credit Card List screen, and as editable when arriving from any other source.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Screen attributes are being set up (1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Cursor positioning is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is TRUE or FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK is TRUE, the cursor is placed on the Account ID field (ACCTSIDL of CCRDSLAI set to -1). If FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK is TRUE or FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK is TRUE, the cursor is placed on the Card Number field (CARDSIDL of CCRDSLAI set to -1). In all other cases (WHEN OTHER), the cursor defaults to the Account ID field (ACCTSIDL of CCRDSLAI set to -1)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Cursor Positioning Based on Validation State
all_rules.Rule_Description: The cursor is automatically positioned on the field that requires the user's attention based on the current validation state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Screen attributes are being set up (1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Field color setup executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET equals LIT-CCLISTMAPSET AND CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM equals LIT-CCLISTPGM, both ACCTSIDC and CARDSIDC of CCRDSLAO are set to DFHDFCOL (default color). If FLG-ACCTFILTER-NOT-OK is TRUE, ACCTSIDC of CCRDSLAO is set to DFHRED (red). If FLG-CARDFILTER-NOT-OK is TRUE, CARDSIDC of CCRDSLAO is set to DFHRED (red)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Field Color Setup Based on Validation Results
all_rules.Rule_Description: Field colors on the screen are set based on the source of navigation and validation results. Fields from the Card List screen use default color, while invalid fields are highlighted in red.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Screen attributes are being set up (1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS) and the program is in re-entry state (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: FLG-ACCTFILTER-BLANK is TRUE AND CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE, or FLG-CARDFILTER-BLANK is TRUE AND CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is TRUE
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For a blank Account ID: '*' is moved to ACCTSIDO of CCRDSLAO and ACCTSIDC of CCRDSLAO is set to DFHRED (red highlight). For a blank Card Number: '*' is moved to CARDSIDO of CCRDSLAO and CARDSIDC of CCRDSLAO is set to DFHRED (red highlight)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Blank Field Red Highlight with Asterisk on Re-Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user re-submits the screen with blank Account ID or Card Number fields, an asterisk is displayed in the blank field and the field is highlighted in red to visually indicate the missing required value.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Screen attributes are being set up (1300-SETUP-SCREEN-ATTRS)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Info message color setup executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If WS-NO-INFO-MESSAGE is TRUE (no informational message available), INFOMSGC of CCRDSLAO is set to DFHBMDAR (dark/dim color). Otherwise, INFOMSGC of CCRDSLAO is set to DFHNEUTR (neutral color) to display the informational message normally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Informational Message Area Color Setting
all_rules.Rule_Description: The color of the informational message area on the screen is set based on whether an informational message is available to display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All screen fields, attributes, and colors have been set up
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Screen transmission (1400-SEND-SCREEN) executes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current mapset (LIT-THISMAPSET) is set as CCARD-NEXT-MAPSET, the current map (LIT-THISMAP) is set as CCARD-NEXT-MAP, CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is set to TRUE (marking the program for re-entry on next user action), and the screen (CCRDSLAO) is sent to the terminal with cursor positioning, screen erase, and keyboard unlock

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Transmission to User Terminal
all_rules.Rule_Description: The fully formatted Credit Card Detail screen is sent to the user's terminal, and the program state is set to re-entry mode to handle the user's next input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen has been sent to the user terminal and the program is ready to return
Acceptance_Criteria.When: COMMON-RETURN is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: WS-RETURN-MSG is moved to CCARD-ERROR-MSG, CARDDEMO-COMMAREA is moved to WS-COMMAREA, WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA is moved into WS-COMMAREA starting at the position after CARDDEMO-COMMAREA (offset: LENGTH OF CARDDEMO-COMMAREA + 1, for LENGTH OF WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA bytes), and control is returned to CICS with the transaction ID LIT-THISTRANID and the packaged WS-COMMAREA as the communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return with Session Context Preservation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After sending the screen, the program packages all session data into the communication area and returns control to CICS, awaiting the user's next action under the same transaction ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is evaluating the current key or program state
Acceptance_Criteria.When: None of the defined states match (WHEN OTHER): not PF3, not first-entry from Card List, not first-entry general, and not re-entry
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: LIT-THISPGM is moved to ABEND-CULPRIT, error code '0001' is moved to ABEND-CODE, ABEND-REASON is set to SPACES, the message 'UNEXPECTED DATA SCENARIO' is moved to WS-RETURN-MSG, and the plain text error message is sent to the terminal (SEND-PLAIN-TEXT) followed by program termination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Unexpected Program State Handling
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program encounters an unexpected state that does not match any defined processing scenario, an error condition is raised with a specific error code and message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Credit Card Detail program (CCRDSL) has been invoked and is beginning execution
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program starts its initialization sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All working storage areas (CC-WORK-AREA and WS-MISC-STORAGE) must be reset to their initial default values, ensuring no stale or residual data from any prior program execution is carried forward into the current session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Working Storage Areas at Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the start of the Credit Card Detail program, all working storage areas used for card data processing and miscellaneous storage must be cleared to ensure no residual data from previous executions affects the current session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Credit Card Detail program (CCRDSL) has been invoked and working storage areas have been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program continues its initialization sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The communication area working storage (WS-COMMAREA) must be reset to its initial default values, ensuring no residual inter-program communication data from prior executions is present before the program loads the actual communication area data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Communication Area Storage at Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the start of the Credit Card Detail program, the communication area working storage (WS-COMMAREA) must be cleared to ensure a clean state before any session data is loaded or exchanged with other programs.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Credit Card Detail program (CCRDSL) has been invoked and storage areas have been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program sets up its session identity during initialization
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program's own transaction identifier (LIT-THISTRANID) must be stored in the working storage transaction ID field (WS-TRANID), establishing the current transaction context for the duration of this program session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Current Transaction ID for This Program Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: At program initialization, the system must record the current transaction identifier (LIT-THISTRANID) into the working storage transaction ID field (WS-TRANID) so that the program can correctly identify and reference itself throughout the session, including during navigation and return operations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Credit Card Detail program (CCRDSL) has been invoked and the transaction ID has been set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program completes its initialization sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The return message flag (WS-RETURN-MSG-OFF) must be set to TRUE (OFF state), meaning no return message will be shown to the user by default; a message will only appear if a subsequent business rule or validation condition explicitly sets one during the current program execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Return Message to OFF as Default at Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: At program initialization, the return message indicator must be set to OFF by default, ensuring that no error or informational message is displayed to the user unless a specific business condition explicitly triggers one during the current session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is accessing the Credit Card Detail screen and no prior session data exists (communication area length is zero), indicating this is the very first interaction with the application
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is loaded with no previously passed session information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All session data must be initialized to empty/default values, including: the account ID is cleared, the card number is cleared, and all program context information (current program, transaction IDs, re-entry flags, user type) is reset to initial empty state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fresh Session Initialization on First Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user accesses the Credit Card Detail screen for the very first time with no prior session data, all session information including account ID, card number, and program context must be cleared and initialized to empty values to ensure a clean starting state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has prior session data available (communication area length is greater than zero) AND the originating program is identified as the Main Menu program AND the program re-entry flag is NOT set (meaning this is a fresh navigation, not a return)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is loaded after navigation from the Main Menu
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All session data must be initialized to empty/default values, including: the account ID is cleared, the card number is cleared, and all program context information (current program, transaction IDs, re-entry flags, user type) is reset to initial empty state — identical to a first-time entry

all_rules.Rule_Name: Fresh Session Initialization When Arriving from Main Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user navigates to the Credit Card Detail screen directly from the Main Menu (not as a re-entry), all session data must be cleared and re-initialized to ensure no stale data from a previous session is carried forward.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is returning to the Credit Card Detail screen AND prior session data exists (communication area length is greater than zero) AND the originating program is NOT the Main Menu OR the program re-entry flag IS set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen is loaded as a return from a prior interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The account ID and all associated session data stored in the main communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) — including account ID, card number, transaction IDs, program names, and user type — are restored from the previously passed communication area data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Restore Account ID from Prior Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user returns to the Credit Card Detail screen from a screen other than the Main Menu (e.g., returning from a downstream screen), the previously entered or selected account ID must be restored from the saved session data so the user does not need to re-enter it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is returning to the Credit Card Detail screen AND prior session data exists (communication area length is greater than zero) AND the originating program is NOT the Main Menu OR the program re-entry flag IS set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The main communication area data is loaded from the previously passed session
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card number previously entered or selected by the user is restored from the main communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), making it available for display and processing on the screen without requiring the user to re-enter it

all_rules.Rule_Name: Restore Card Number from Prior Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user returns to the Credit Card Detail screen from a prior interaction, the previously entered or selected card number must be restored from the saved session data as part of the main communication area restoration, ensuring continuity of the user's search context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is returning to the Credit Card Detail screen AND prior session data exists (communication area length is greater than zero) AND the originating program is NOT the Main Menu OR the program re-entry flag IS set AND the main communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) has already been restored
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program-specific communication area segment is loaded from the previously passed session data, starting immediately after the main communication area portion
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program-specific context data (WS-THIS-PROGCOMMAREA) — containing screen-level state, field validation flags, and any other data specific to the Credit Card Detail screen — is restored from the second segment of the passed communication area, completing the full session restoration

all_rules.Rule_Name: Restore Program Context from Prior Session
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user returns to the Credit Card Detail screen from a prior interaction, the program-specific context data (such as screen state, validation flags, and field-level data specific to this screen) must be restored from the saved session to maintain the exact state the user was in before navigating away.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Credit Card Detail screen and presses any key on the terminal keyboard
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system receives the key input from the terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system evaluates the key pressed and stores it as one of the following recognized key identifiers: Enter Key, Clear Key, PA1, PA2, PF1 through PF12 — so that the stored key identifier is available for all subsequent screen processing logic

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture and Store User Function Key Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user interacts with the Credit Card Detail screen, the system must capture and internally record which function key was pressed so that subsequent processing can determine the appropriate action to take.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Credit Card Detail screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any function key in the range PF13 through PF24
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system maps and stores the key as its PF01-PF12 equivalent as follows: PF13 is stored as PF01, PF14 as PF02, PF15 as PF03, PF16 as PF04, PF17 as PF05, PF18 as PF06, PF19 as PF07, PF20 as PF08, PF21 as PF09, PF22 as PF10, PF23 as PF11, and PF24 as PF12 — so that the behavior is identical to pressing the corresponding lower-range function key

all_rules.Rule_Name: Map Extended Function Keys PF13-PF24 to PF01-PF12 Equivalents
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Credit Card Detail screen treats the upper range of function keys (PF13 through PF24) as direct equivalents of PF01 through PF12. This ensures consistent behavior regardless of whether the user presses the primary or secondary set of function keys.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has pressed a key on the Credit Card Detail screen and the key has been captured and stored
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the stored key identifier against the list of acceptable keys for this screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the stored key is the Enter key OR PF3 key, the key is marked as VALID and acceptable for this screen; for all other stored keys including Clear, PA1, PA2, PF1, PF2, PF4 through PF12, the key is marked as INVALID and not acceptable for this screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify Acceptable Keys for the Credit Card Detail Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Credit Card Detail screen only accepts two specific key inputs as valid actions: the Enter key (to submit or confirm) and PF3 (to navigate back). All other keys are considered invalid for this screen and are not accepted as intentional user actions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has pressed a key on the Credit Card Detail screen and the key has been evaluated and marked as INVALID (i.e., it is not the Enter key or PF3)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the pressed key is marked as INVALID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system overrides the stored key identifier and replaces it with the Enter key identifier, so that all subsequent processing treats the user's action as if the Enter key had been pressed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Override Invalid Key Press to Default Enter Key Behavior
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses a key that is not recognized as valid for the Credit Card Detail screen, the system must not halt or produce an error. Instead, it silently overrides the unrecognized key action and defaults to Enter key behavior, ensuring the screen continues to process normally.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has pressed a key on the Credit Card Detail screen and the key has been evaluated and marked as VALID (i.e., it is the Enter key or PF3)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the pressed key is marked as VALID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retains the stored key identifier unchanged — Enter key remains as Enter key and PF3 remains as PF3 — so that the correct corresponding action is executed in subsequent processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve Valid Key Press Without Override
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses a key that is recognized as valid for the Credit Card Detail screen (Enter or PF3), the system retains the originally stored key identifier without any modification, ensuring the intended user action is honored.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user is on the Credit Card Detail screen and presses any key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system captures the key pressed, mapping: ENTER to Enter indicator, CLEAR to Clear indicator, PA1 to PA1 indicator, PA2 to PA2 indicator, PF1-PF12 to their respective PFK01-PFK12 indicators, and PF13-PF24 mapped equivalently to PFK01-PFK12 indicators
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The corresponding logical key indicator (CCARD-AID-ENTER, CCARD-AID-CLEAR, CCARD-AID-PA1, CCARD-AID-PA2, CCARD-AID-PFK01 through CCARD-AID-PFK12) is set to TRUE to represent the key that was pressed, and processing continues to key validation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture and Identify the Key Pressed by User
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses any key on the Credit Card Detail screen, the system identifies and records which specific key was pressed by mapping the physical key input to a logical key indicator. Function keys PF13 through PF24 are treated as equivalent to PF01 through PF12 respectively.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has pressed a key on the Credit Card Detail screen and the key has been captured and identified
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins the key validation process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key validity status is set to INVALID (PFK-INVALID = TRUE) as the default assumption before any further validation is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default All Keys to Invalid Before Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before evaluating which key was pressed, the system pre-emptively marks the key action as invalid. This ensures that only explicitly supported keys are permitted to drive screen processing, and any unrecognized key is caught by default.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has pressed a key on the Credit Card Detail screen and the key validity status has been defaulted to INVALID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the key pressed was the ENTER key (CCARD-AID-ENTER is TRUE) OR the PF3 key (CCARD-AID-PFK03 is TRUE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the key pressed was ENTER or PF3, the key validity status is updated to VALID (PFK-VALID = TRUE) and normal screen processing continues with the recognized key action

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Supported Keys - Enter and PF3 Only
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Credit Card Detail screen only supports two valid user actions: pressing the ENTER key to submit or process data, and pressing PF3 to navigate back. All other keys are not recognized as valid actions for this screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has pressed either the ENTER key or the PF3 key on the Credit Card Detail screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the key is one of the two supported keys (ENTER or PF3)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The key validity status is set to VALID (PFK-VALID = TRUE) and the system proceeds with normal screen processing using the action associated with the pressed key

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Key as Valid and Continue Normal Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a supported key (ENTER or PF3) is confirmed as pressed, the system marks the key as valid and allows normal screen processing to proceed with the intended action associated with that key.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has pressed a key on the Credit Card Detail screen that is not the ENTER key and not the PF3 key (e.g., CLEAR, PA1, PA2, PF1, PF2, PF4 through PF12, or any other function key)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks the key validity status and finds it is still INVALID (PFK-INVALID = TRUE), meaning neither ENTER nor PF3 was pressed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system overrides the key action by setting the ENTER key indicator to TRUE (CCARD-AID-ENTER = TRUE), effectively treating the unsupported key press as an ENTER key press, and normal screen processing continues as if the user had pressed ENTER

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Unsupported Key Action to Enter Key Behavior
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses any key other than ENTER or PF3 on the Credit Card Detail screen, the system does not reject the interaction. Instead, it silently overrides the unsupported key action and treats it as if the user had pressed the ENTER key, ensuring uninterrupted screen processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the Credit Card Detail screen and the session context may or may not contain an originating transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF3 (Exit key)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the originating transaction ID is blank or empty (LOW-VALUES or SPACES), the destination transaction is set to the Main Menu transaction (LIT-MENUTRANID); otherwise, the destination transaction is set to the originating transaction ID (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID) that was recorded when this screen was called

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Destination Transaction on PF3 Exit
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 to exit the Credit Card Detail screen, the system determines which transaction to return to. If no originating transaction is recorded in the session, the user is directed to the Main Menu transaction; otherwise, the user is returned to the transaction that originally called this screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF3 on the Credit Card Detail screen and the session context may or may not contain an originating program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The destination transaction has been resolved and the system now evaluates the originating program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the originating program name is blank or empty (LOW-VALUES or SPACES), the destination program is set to the Main Menu program (LIT-MENUPGM); otherwise, the destination program is set to the originating program name (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM) that was recorded when this screen was called

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Destination Program on PF3 Exit
all_rules.Rule_Description: After determining the destination transaction, the system also determines which program to transfer control to. If no originating program is recorded in the session, the user is directed to the Main Menu program; otherwise, the user is returned to the program that originally called this screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF3 and the destination transaction and program have been determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control to the destination program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The navigation context is updated so that: the current transaction ID (LIT-THISTRANID) is recorded as the originating transaction (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), the current program name (LIT-THISPGM) is recorded as the originating program (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), the current map set name (LIT-THISMAPSET) is recorded as the last map set used (CDEMO-LAST-MAPSET), and the current map name (LIT-THISMAP) is recorded as the last map used (CDEMO-LAST-MAP)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Update Navigation Context Before PF3 Exit
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the destination program, the system records the current screen's identity as the source of this navigation. This ensures the destination program knows where the user came from, enabling correct back-navigation if needed. The current transaction ID, program name, map set, and map name are all recorded in the shared navigation context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The navigation context has been updated with the current screen's identity and the destination program has been determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is about to transfer control to the destination program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program entry state is set to fresh entry mode (CDEMO-PGM-ENTER = TRUE) so the destination program treats this as a new entry, and the user type is set to standard user (CDEMO-USRTYP-USER = TRUE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Fresh Entry Mode for Destination Program on PF3 Exit
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating back via PF3, the destination program must receive the user in a fresh entry state rather than a re-entry state. The user type is also set to standard user. This ensures the destination program presents a clean initial screen rather than attempting to re-process previously submitted data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) has been determined, the navigation context has been updated, and the user entry mode has been set to fresh entry
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the program transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is transferred to the destination program (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM) with the full navigation communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) passed along, and the current Credit Card Detail screen program terminates its execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Destination Program on PF3 Exit
